children: investments in price, innovation, and marketing are starting to pay off, and the “seesaw” performance in the past will tilt in the company’s favor in 2027 as growth will more than offset the impact from its declining businesses. This earned the company an Outperform rating at RBC Capital and a $32 price target, representing 36% upside to its last closing price.

“We believe 2026 has provided tangible proof points that current actions in motion are having a positive benefit,” RBC analyst Nik Modi writes in his note to clients, adding that he expects further improvement over the remainder of this year with more of a “step-function change” in 2027.

Modi cites innovations like PowerMac and Capri Sun Hydrate as two innovations that are addressing real consumer needs rather than defending shelf space. The company has also implemented strategic price cuts, introduced smaller packaging, and increased in-store promotions,
“We believe investors have assumed the [innovation] progress will stall. We disagree,” Modi says as every discussion with Kraft Heinz
management indicates the innovation slate for 2027 is “robust and strategically focused,” representing a direct result of changes in the company’s R&D process and resource allocation.
The company also appears to have more room for improvement, with recent changes to its incentive structure more closely aligning rewards with market share.
Modi notes that while the 27.5% stake held by Berkshire Hathaway in Kraft Heinz

is an “overhang” on the share price, the impact is “navigable.” Berkshire’s Greg Abel called the KHC investment “disappointing” and is likely looking for an exit. But for Berkshire to sell, Modi thinks the stock price will need to rise.
“So if shares sell off on Berkshire's supply, we would treat that as an opportunity to add.”

title: Kraft-Heinz's investments in new products, affordable prices paying off—RBC Capital
